comment: Mutation testing for the ROUND-27 MEMBER-RESOLUTION PHASES. A fifth config targeting the SAME project as stryker-config.json but a disjoint set of files, because the two measure different things and must not share a floor: the original generator leg guards four small deliberately-chosen files (EquatableArray, BlittableProof, ConstructorSelector, LocationInfo) and has held break 84 for several rounds, and folding new lines into it would collapse that number in a way indistinguishable from a regression in the four it protects. WHY THIS LEG EXISTS: round 27 extracted 13 new Pipeline/ files from three giant methods, and the brief asked for the moved functions to be covered 'close to 100 % from mutation and other standpoints'. Line coverage (94.5 %) and reach (32/32 methods) were delivered; MUTATION coverage of those functions was 0 %, because no leg's mutate globs named any of the new files. WHY ONLY THREE FILES. The first attempt scoped this leg at all 13 extracted files (6,659 lines). Measured 2026-08-27: Stryker generated 13,129 mutants, discarded 3,240 as compile errors and filtered 8,049 as out-of-leg, leaving 1,353 to test -- and after 158 minutes on 12 cores it had not finished, while leaking idle vstest testhost processes (26 of 32 alive with no CPU). That is not a gate anyone can run: it exceeds the nightly CI budget by an order of magnitude, and it did not reliably terminate locally either. The run was abandoned deliberately rather than left to finish, and the cost curve it produced is the evidence for the scoping here. So this leg takes ONE AREA, the way Issues/round27/AUDIT-mutation-scope.md already recommended: the four member-resolution phases (ApplySkipNullSourceMembers, ResolveMapValues, ResolveExplicitMaps, ResolveAutoMatchedMembers) plus the two context records they are parameterised by. MEASURED 2026-08-27 on 12 cores: 236 tested mutants of 13,129 created (9,583 filtered as out-of-leg, 3,240 rolled back as compile errors), 37 minutes wall-clock, 184 detected of 239 scoreable = 76.99 %. The estimate beforehand was ~190 from the abandoned run's density of ~0.20 tested mutants per line; the real figure is 236, and the estimate is recorded here only so the density heuristic can be judged against it when the next area is sized. The other ten extracted files stay uncovered and are named in the audit as the follow-on programme, one area per leg, each with its own measured floor. NOTE -- the mutate globs are PROJECT-relative ('**/Name.cs'), never repo-root-relative: Stryker resolves them against src/DwarfMapper.Generator, so a repo-root path matches nothing, every mutant is dropped with 'Removed by mutate filter', and Stryker STILL EXITS 0. Assert-MutantsWereTested (scripts/housekeeping.ps1) exists for exactly that hazard. NOTE -- files are listed explicitly rather than globbed with 'Pipeline/*.cs', so adding one is a deliberate act that shows up in review AND cannot silently push the leg back over its CI budget; the four sibling configs follow the same convention. NOTE -- break/low are pinned to the FIRST MEASURED score, floored, exactly as the CodeFixes leg was (52.54 -> break 52, later raised to 87 by killing survivors). Raise break only by killing survivors, never by re-measuring on a lucky run; the floor moves in the same commit as the kills that earned it. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-07 (round 29, Phase 2 gate): 78.28 % (191 detected of 242 scoreable -- 191 killed, 0 timeout, 51 survived), so break/low 76 -> 78 and high 79 -> 80, in this commit. This raise is REQUIRED, not opportunistic: gate-checks.ps1 throws when the floored score reaches break + 1 (invariant R2 -- the floor must equal the measurement), so 78 was not a choice. It also does not contradict the note above it, which forbids CHASING a raise by re-running until a run is lucky; the two rules address different things, and this run is not a lucky one -- the Timeout bucket is ZERO, which is the first thing R2's own error text says to check, because a timeout counts as detected and a re-classification would move the score with no test having changed. The rise from the first pinned 76 is credited to round 29's own work: Phase 2 and the six defect tasks added tests directly over this leg's mutate set (MapperExtractor.Members.Phases.cs among them, which task 2.7 changed and covered). Determinism evidence from the same gate run: the CodeFixes leg reproduced its round-27 figure EXACTLY (154 killed / 19 survived / 87.01 %) across ten days and a full round of generator change. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-09 (round 29, Phase 3 gate): 89.80 % (273 detected of 304 scoreable -- 273 killed, 0 timeout, 29 survived, 2 not covered by any test), so break/low 78 -> 89 and high 80 -> 90, in this commit. THIS RAISE IS EARNED BY KILLS, NOT BY A LUCKY RUN, and the evidence is a mutant-by-mutant diff of the two reports rather than a pair of headline numbers: against the previous run over the identical 646-mutant population, EVERY status change is in one direction -- 33 Survived -> Killed and 9 NoCoverage -> Killed, and NOT ONE Killed -> Survived. The Timeout bucket is zero in both, which is the first thing R2's own error text says to check. Sixteen of the 42 new kills sit on lines 365-367 and 403-405, the four-way ternaries naming which [MapProperty] modifier conflicts with a share or a dense fill; the commit that earned them is 7d50320, eight [Theory] tests of four arms each. WHY THE FLOOR MOVES ONE COMMIT LATER THAN THE KILLS, against the rule above it: this leg takes 34 minutes, so the confirming measurement cannot exist inside the commit that writes the tests. The rule's intent -- that a raise be backed by kills rather than by re-rolling -- is met; its letter is not, and saying so here is cheaper than pretending the two landed together. WHAT THE FIRST PHASE 3 ATTEMPT FOUND, because it is the reason any of this happened: that run scored 75.99 % -- BELOW the then-floor of 78 -- with 11 mutants NoCoverage clustered on those same ternaries. Both of round 29's new attributes shipped with their 'which modifier' refusal branch NEVER EXECUTED by any of the 7,838 tests then green. Only the mutation tier saw it. REMAINING HEADROOM IS TWO MUTANTS: 89 % of 304 requires 271 detected and 273 are, so a three-mutant regression reds this gate. That is the ratchet working as designed, and the 29 survivors plus 2 NoCoverage -- all in MapperExtractor.Members.Phases.cs -- are the next kill programme's worklist, recorded in Issues/ledgers/equivalent-mutants.md.
